opening_question_spark: Why is airflow strongest beside a broken airplane window?
book_transition: Higher cabin pressure gives the first clue.
cta: Follow for more clear flight answers.
body: Outside pressure is lower at high altitude.
A broken window lets cabin air rush out.
Air moves fastest near the opening.
Farther away, it may move much less.
Cabin pressure falls, making breathing harder.
Masks may drop as pilots descend quickly.
optional_closing: That is decompression, with the strongest airflow near the break.
